SMTO-HTTP-0024 — Signed in, but SMTO couldn't find the session it needs

GUID: 72e83530-98ac-4ded-816f-870b949be775
Slug: http-session-mapping-required
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • The web service accepted the login, but its reply didn't include the session cookie or value the saved connection tells SMTO to look for. Your password was not rejected; the connection's login settings need adjusting.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check the service's documentation to see what its login sends back: a cookie (and its name), or a value such as a token in the reply or a header. SMTO needs to know exactly where the service puts the session after you log in.
  2. Open Parameter Store and select the connection. Under Session cookie, set Cookie name. Or, under Advanced login settings, add an Extracted value with its Source and Extraction path. These settings tell SMTO where to find the session in the login reply.
  3. Under Advanced login settings, check that Login success codes list only the replies the service gives for a successful login. If a failed login uses the same code, SMTO treats it as success and then finds no session.
  4. Select Save, then select Test connection. The test signs in again and confirms SMTO can now find the session.

What success looks like

  • Test connection succeeds and SMTO's requests to the service return results.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the service's login documentation, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't change the password; it was not rejected.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The session-login request returned a configured success status, but a configured extraction rule failed or no extracted value or session cookie was obtained.

What this means

  • Login returned a configured success status but required extraction failed, or neither extracted values nor session cookies were available. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Login returned a configured success status but required extraction failed, or neither extracted values nor session cookies were available.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the sanitized successful response shape with configured JSON/header/cookie mappings; the code explicitly does not establish credential rejection.

How to fix it

  • The login returned its expected success status. SessionLogin.prepare_session (gateway_core/http_auth/providers.py) raises this when an extract rule (JSON pointer, header or cookie) fails, or when no extracted values and no session cookies were obtained. Configure extraction/session mapping (login extract rules or session_cookie) from the actual documented response; this is not proof of rejected credentials.
  • The login returned its expected success status. Configure extraction/session mapping from the actual documented response; this is not proof of rejected credentials.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • Required session values or cookies are extracted and the intended resource probe confirms the session.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.
